fact: CINX, the Cape Town Internet Exchange run by INX-ZA, is in service with 122 connected networks on 153 ports across six Cape Town data-centre locations, per INX-ZA's IX-F member export of 10 August 2026; two new OADC nodes (Rondebosch, Bellville) went live per its 3 August 2026 announcement.

Microsoft, Cloudflare, Akamai, Meta and Fastly hold 100 Gbps ports at CINX Cape Town (Teraco Rondebosch), and Amazon holds 100 Gbps at Africa Data Centres Diep Rivier, per INX-ZA's member export of 10 August 2026.
Content delivery network CDN77 has joined JINX Johannesburg as a new member since March 2026, per the article.
South Africa has two exchanges in different cities run by INX-ZA: CINX in Cape Town (122 networks) and JINX in Johannesburg (208 networks), per INX-ZA's member export of 10 August 2026.
Teraco says its Cape Town campus offers seamless peering via the NAPAfrica internet exchange point; no member count or traffic is given.
Teraco says its Cape Town CT2 data centre gives clients peering via the NAPAfrica internet exchange point (date taken from the article, 2025-11-10).

Teraco says its data centres, including JB4 in Ekurhuleni east of Johannesburg, give access to peering at NAPAfrica, which it calls the eighth largest internet exchange in the world, and to regional IXPs (date taken from the release, 2025-08-12).
Equinix says the INX-ZA Johannesburg Internet Exchange (JINX) is already established at its new JN1 data centre in Germiston, Johannesburg, opened on 24 October 2024.

Connecting Africa reports that Africa Data Centres' CPT1 facility in Cape Town houses the Cape Town Internet Exchange (CINX), which it says makes multi-region peering easier (date taken from the article, 2024-07-25).

Teraco states that clients at its DB1 Durban facility have direct peering at NAPAfrica, which it calls Africa's largest internet exchange point.
Teraco states that its Isando campus data centres in Ekurhuleni, Johannesburg already provide peering at NAPAfrica and regional IXPs.
Digital Realty states that Teraco owns NAPAfrica, which it calls the continent's largest internet exchange point.

Teraco states that clients in its Cape Town CT1 and CT2 data centres have direct peering at NAPAfrica, which it calls Africa's largest internet exchange point, within an ecosystem of over 250 network providers.
